items.html: The warm re-run passed in 716 s (11.9 min). Cache restore took 3–10 s. Updating the PR description with the measured numbers.

I pushed the branch and opened draft PR #2. On GitHub it brought a CI run from a 19.0 min median down to 11.9 min with a warm cache, and 15.2 min when the cache is cold. Both runs were fully green.

Wall-clock
Before (median of 5 runs, 15.5–21.5 min) 19.0 min
This PR, cold cache (first run) 15.2 min
This PR, warm cache (re-run) 11.9 min

That's one sample of each, and runner speed varies by about 1.5x between runs. The warm result matches the projection (12–13.5 min).

Confirmed on real runners

  • Python lanes: the Python 3.12 lane plus Coverage now finishes about 6 min into the run, down from about 14.5 min.
  • xdist: it passed on every pytest lane: 3.12–3.15, the NumPy lanes and the lower-bounds lane. Test steps take about half as long as before.
  • macOS cache: restoring takes 3–10 s, and saving takes 8–13 s for about 140 MB per platform.
  • Intel cross-build: the wheel has tag macosx_10_12_x86_64. It was built on macos-26-arm64 in 226–328 s, against 393–1010 s natively on Intel, and smoke-tested on real x86_64 macos-15 runners. GitHub accepted the YAML anchors.

Not verified

  • What happens to the Intel smoke tests when an unrelated wheel build fails.
  • main's first push after merging will run cold. It saves the cache that later PRs start from.

What sets the time now

  • The Intel smoke tests wait for all 20 wheel builds before they start.
  • Installing the Python 3.15 prerelease on Intel takes about 2 min. That should go away once 3.15.0 final ships on GitHub's runner images.
  • The 5-job macOS cap still causes some queueing.
  • After macOS, the next bound is the Windows wheels at about 8 min.
  • Two settings would help without any code: raising cache retention past 7 days (so quiet weeks don't start cold), and asking GitHub Support for a higher macOS limit.

The PR description now includes the measured numbers. No reviewers are requested and it's still a draft. GitHub doesn't require any approval for main; the only required check, CI Success, passes. Taking it out of draft and merging is up to you. I'll keep treams-ci-speed until it merges, then remove it.
